tagline: Wheat by rail, and an older village of fur traders.
intro: Along US 12 between Wallula and Walla Walla, Lowden sits among family farms and wineries. The railroad from Wallula was not finished to Walla Walla until 1875, but its track reached Touchet in March 1874, and by the end of that year Touchet farmers had shipped 4,000 tons of wheat.

Frenchtown is older than all of it. French Canadian and Métis fur traders built the first cabins in the 1820s, and the community scattered after the army ordered residents out of the valley in 1855 and fighting followed. Its historic site keeps the Saint Rose of Lima cemetery.

moments.title: Touchet
moments.text: The name comes from Tuushi, a Walla Walla village near the townsite, meaning baking salmon on sticks over coals.

moments.title: Lowden
moments.text: The community nearest old Frenchtown kept that name until 1915, when it was renamed for farmer and rancher Francis M. Lowden.

moments.title: Frenchtown
moments.text: The restored Prince's cabin, built around 1837 near the Whitman Mission for a Cayuse man the Hudson's Bay Company called the Prince, now stands at the historic site.
